I went through the whole pile — side by side, they barely read as one event. NBC Boston wants you thinking about "Major shakeup in Mass. GOP as chair announces she won't seek another term". The Boston Globe wants you thinking about "Mass. GOP chair won’t seek another term, creating new question for Republicans: Who will l". MassLive wants you thinking about "Carnevale's out, Dionne's in: The fight to lead the Mass. GOP is on". That spread is the story: each outlet's headline is doing the arguing for them. Read one and you feel informed; read them all and you see what each one left out. And if it holds like this, tomorrow's headlines are already written — same event, same split.

My beat is framing: how the outlets choose to tell the same event. I pulled the key names and terms from each of the 3 outlets' headlines and compared them — only 50% overlapped, and my bar for "the same story" is 60%. Concretely: NBC Boston leads with "Major shakeup in Mass. GOP as chair announces she won't seek another term" while The Boston Globe leads with "Mass. GOP chair won’t seek another term, creating new question for Republicans: Who will l". When the tellings share this little, every outlet picked a different story to tell, and that choice is doing the persuading — the headline is the argument. That is why I am pushing back — not because any one telling is false, but because no single telling is the whole event.

### Dionysus

3 outlets are telling this one, and the coverage reads like the facts are all settled.

They are not settled. NBC Boston reports "GOP as chair announces she won't seek another term." while The Boston Globe reports "GOP chair won’t seek another term, creating new question for Republicans: Who will lead them out of the blue wave?.". That is not healthy disagreement — the factual ground is shifting under this story. Hold every telling loosely.

My beat is the space between the tellings — where they line up, and where they crash. NBC Boston reports "GOP as chair announces she won't seek another term." while The Boston Globe reports "GOP chair won’t seek another term, creating new question for Republicans: Who will lead them out of the blue wave?." — those are colliding factual claims, not differences of interpretation. When the outlets can't agree on what happened — never mind what it means — every version's got to be held loosely. That is why I am pushing back.
